reason: Empty Content-Length header ("") with maxSize: -1: original parses '0' -> 0 > -1 -> onError (413); mutant parses '' -> NaN -> next()
Default onError: the thrown HTTPException's res has status 200 instead of 413; an app.onError that returns err.res (public field) sees 200 (getResponse() still uses 413)

Content-Length-only path removed: request with Content-Length: 1000 but a 5-byte body and maxSize 100 is rejected originally without reading the body, mutant streams it and passes; also body is read/rewrapped even when within limit
Same as 20: Content-Length larger than maxSize while actual body is smaller -> original 413 without reading, mutant reads the stream and passes
cors({ allowMethods: undefined }) (explicit undefined overrides default): mutant leaves findAllowMethods undefined, so a preflight throws TypeError instead of returning 204 without Allow-Methods
Fallback returns undefined instead of ''; both are falsy and the only use is `if (allowMethods)`, so no header is set either way
cors({ allowMethods: undefined }): preflight gets 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods: Stryker was here!' instead of no header
Request without Origin and a function origin (e.g. o => o || 'fallback') or array containing '': the function receives 'Stryker was here!' instead of '', changing Allow-Origin
Default options: every response gets 'Access-Control-Expose-Headers: undefined'
Default options (credentials unset): response gets 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'
Preflight with default origin '*': mutant appends 'Vary: Origin'
Preflight without Origin and a function allowMethods: it receives 'Stryker was here!' instead of '' as origin, so a function that branches on origin returns different methods
allowHeaders ['X-A'] and preflight with Access-Control-Request-Headers: X-B: mutant answers 'X-B' instead of 'X-A'
Preflight with default origin '*': '*' !== '' is true so mutant appends 'Vary: Origin'
Preflight with no allowHeaders and no Access-Control-Request-Headers: mutant sets 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers: undefined' and appends Vary
Default allowHeaders: preflight gets 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Stryker was here' instead of echoing the request headers / no header
cors({ exposeHeaders: undefined }) (allowed by the optional type): mutant throws TypeError reading .length at construction
cors({ allowHeaders: undefined }): mutant throws TypeError reading .length at construction
cors({ allowMethods: undefined }): mutant calls undefined.join and throws at construction instead of yielding no Allow-Methods header
offset 0 branch runs only for a CSP directive key whose first char is uppercase; every key of ContentSecurityPolicyOptions starts lowercase, so unreachable through the typed API
permissionsPolicy: { camera: undefined, geolocation: true } (Partial allows undefined): original filters the '' out, mutant emits 'Stryker was here!' in Permissions-Policy
Default parameter of getReportingEndpoints is never used: its only caller is guarded by `if (options.reportingEndpoints)`, so the argument is always truthy
Default parameter of getReportToOptions is never used: its only caller is guarded by `if (options.reportTo)`, so the argument is always truthy
With a NONCE directive, generateNonce returns undefined -> CSP contains 'nonce-undefined' and secureHeadersNonce is undefined
Without getRandomValues the nonce is always the base64 of 16 zero bytes, identical across requests (predictable nonce)
CSP with NONCE: header contains 'nonce-true' instead of a random nonce
CSP with NONCE and no preset nonce: init && ... yields undefined -> 'nonce-undefined'
CSP with NONCE: header contains 'nonce-false' instead of a random nonce
Handler sets c.set('secureHeadersNonce','') beforehand: original keeps '' on the context while emitting a generated nonce; mutant overwrites the context with the generated nonce
Default options: mutant always sets an empty 'Reporting-Endpoints' header
Default options: mutant always sets an empty 'Report-To' header
options is always an object built from spread of DEFAULT_OPTIONS, so ?. vs . on it never differs
callbacks.reduce over an empty array with initial value headersToSet returns headersToSet, same as the short-circuit branch
[A-Z]+ vs [A-Z] only differs for consecutive capitals in a CSP directive key; no key of ContentSecurityPolicyOptions has consecutive capitals, so kebab output is identical

Lookahead (?=[a-z]) vs (?![a-z]) only differs for a capital not followed by a lowercase letter; in every typed CSP key each capital is followed by a lowercase letter, and the [A-Z] alternative yields the same single-letter match
(?![^a-z]) only differs from (?![a-z]) at end of string or before a non-letter; every capital in typed CSP keys is followed by a lowercase letter, so matches and output are identical

Static CSP is returned as [callback, array] instead of [undefined, string]; the callback runs every request with no inner callbacks and joins the array to the same string, so emitted headers are identical
permissionsPolicy with two directives: mutant drops .filter(Boolean).join(', ') so the header is the array stringified as 'camera=(),microphone=()' instead of 'camera=(), microphone=()'
permissionsPolicy: { camera: undefined }: mutant reads undefined.length and throws at construction instead of omitting the directive
Empty array falls through to the allowlist branch which produces `${k}=()` from an empty join, same as the early return
Same as 415: removing the early return for [] leads to `${k}=(${''})` = `${k}=()`, identical output
permissionsPolicy: { camera: ['*', 'self'] }: mutant returns 'camera=*' instead of 'camera=("*" self)'
permissionsPolicy: { camera: ['none', 'self'] }: mutant returns 'camera=()' instead of 'camera=("none" self)'

[a-z\d] vs [a-z\D] differs only for digit+capital (no match) or capital+capital (extra dash); no PermissionsPolicyDirective key has either (only digit key chUaWow64 ends in digits), so output is identical
secureHeaders() with defaults: mutant sets 'Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp', which must be absent by default
